question: Should an explicit Automation `toolsAllow: []` bypass inherited ordinary allowlists while continuing to enforce only sources marked `enforceWhenToolsDisabled`?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the fail-closed boundary for inherited tool policy; tests and runtime proof show the implementation, but the permanent policy interpretation needs owner confirmation.

options.title: Accept explicit tool-less semantics
options.body: Approve the proposed distinction: explicit `toolsAllow: []` means zero callable tools and skips inherited sources that are not explicitly enforced when tools are disabled.

options.title: Preserve inherited allowlist enforcement
options.body: Keep the existing guard behavior and define a separate, explicit configuration or policy mechanism if tool-less runs need an exception.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit tool-less semantics
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed distinction: explicit `toolsAllow: []` means zero callable tools and skips inherited sources that are not explicitly enforced when tools are disabled.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only directly evidenced participant connected to the reported scenario and proposed boundary; repository ownership history should be added by the human reviewer.
